title: Open-cover descent of sheaves of topological commutative rings
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $A$ a set and $X=\bigcup_{a\in A}U_a$ an open cover. A sheaf of topological commutative rings means a presheaf of commutative topological rings and continuous unital ring homomorphisms for which, for every open covering $W=\bigcup_bW_b$, the map from sections on $W$ to compatible tuples in $\prod_b\mathcal F(W_b)$ is an isomorphism of topological rings, using the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology] from the product. A morphism of such sheaves is a natural transformation whose components are continuous unital ring homomorphisms. Suppose $\mathcal F_a$ is such a sheaf on $U_a$, with isomorphisms $\theta_{ab}:\mathcal F_a|_{U_a\cap U_b}\to\mathcal F_b|_{U_a\cap U_b}$ satisfying $\theta_{aa}=1$ and $\theta_{bc}\theta_{ab}=\theta_{ac}$ on every triple overlap. There exists a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ with isomorphisms $e_a:\mathcal F|_{U_a}\to\mathcal F_a$ satisfying $\theta_{ab}e_a=e_b$ on overlaps. It can be chosen so that for every open $W$, $\mathcal F(W)$ is exactly the ring of compatible tuples $(s_a)\in\prod_a\mathcal F_a(W\cap U_a)$ with its subspace topology and componentwise restrictions. For any two sheaves of topological commutative rings $\mathcal H,\mathcal G$ on $X$, compatible morphisms $\mathcal H|_{U_a}\to\mathcal G|_{U_a}$ extend to a unique morphism $\mathcal H\to\mathcal G$. Consequently the descended object with the specified $e_a$ is unique up to unique isomorphism. The empty space and empty cover are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA, initial discussion of the equalizer topology on sheaves of topological rings and continuous maps; Tag 00AL, lemma-glue-sheaves, first proof; Tag 00AM, lemma-glue-sheaves-structures; Tag 00AN, lemma-mapping-property-glue. The topological version uses the subspace-of-product topology of 0AHY, rather than applying the algebraic-structures claim to topological rings.

proof.text: We use the following immediate continuity test for the specified subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. If $S\subseteq\prod_iT_i$ and $f:Z\to S$, then $f$ is continuous exactly when each coordinate $f_i:Z\to T_i$ is continuous: a subbasic open of $S$ is $S\cap\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}(V)$ for $V\subseteq T_i$ open, whose inverse image is $f_i^{-1}(V)$. Finite intersections and arbitrary unions give all opens. In particular, coordinate projections and maps obtained by composing continuous coordinate maps are continuous. This test includes empty products.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA: subspace of the product topology; elementary subbasis argument

proof.text: For each open $W\subseteq X$, let $P(W)=\prod_a\mathcal F_a(W\cap U_a)$, and define $\mathcal F(W)$ to consist of those $s\in P(W)$ for which $\theta_{ab}(s_a|_{W\cap U_a\cap U_b})=s_b|_{W\cap U_a\cap U_b}$ for every $a,b$. Each condition is an equality of two unital ring homomorphisms, so $0,1$ satisfy it and it is preserved by addition, negation and multiplication. Thus this is a commutative subring, with exactly the claimed set of sections. Give it the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Addition, negation and multiplication are continuous by step 1: their $a$-coordinates are respectively addition, negation and multiplication in $\mathcal F_a(W\cap U_a)$ after the continuous coordinate projections. Hence it is a topological commutative ring. This is the equalizer construction of the source, with the topology imposed explicitly.

source.place: Tags 00AL and 00AM, lemma-glue-sheaves first proof and lemma-glue-sheaves-structures; Tag 0AHY equalizer topology

proof.text: For $W'\subseteq W$, restrict every coordinate from $W\cap U_a$ to $W'\cap U_a$. Naturality of $\theta_{ab}$ preserves each defining compatibility equation, so these are unital ring homomorphisms $\mathcal F(W)\to\mathcal F(W')$. Their coordinates are the continuous local restrictions composed with projections, so step 1 proves continuity. Restriction identities and composition hold in each coordinate and hence for tuples. This defines the required presheaf.

source.place: Tag 00AL, lemma-glue-sheaves, first proof: restriction maps

proof.text: Let $W=\bigcup_bW_b$ and let $t^b\in\mathcal F(W_b)$ be compatible on all $W_b\cap W_c$. For each fixed $a$, the coordinates $t^b_a$ are a compatible family for the cover $W\cap U_a=\bigcup_b(W_b\cap U_a)$. The assumed sheaf axiom of $\mathcal F_a$ supplies a unique $s_a\in\mathcal F_a(W\cap U_a)$ restricting to them. On $W\cap U_a\cap U_c$, the sections $\theta_{ac}(s_a|)$ and $s_c|$ have equal restrictions to every $W_b\cap U_a\cap U_c$, since $t^b$ is a compatible tuple. Injectivity in the sheaf axiom of $\mathcal F_c$ for that cover makes these sections equal. Thus $(s_a)_a\in\mathcal F(W)$ glues the $t^b$, uniquely since each coordinate is uniquely determined. Restriction preserves all ring operations, so the resulting bijection from $\mathcal F(W)$ to compatible families is a unital ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00AL, lemma-glue-sheaves, first proof: the sheaf condition written out

proof.text: Give the compatible families $E\subseteq\prod_b\mathcal F(W_b)$ their subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. The restriction map $\rho:\mathcal F(W)\to E$ is continuous by step 1 and step 3. For its inverse from step 4, fix $a$. The map $E\to\prod_b\mathcal F_a(W_b\cap U_a)$ taking $(t^b)_b$ to $(t^b_a)_b$ is continuous by the subbasis test, as each coordinate is a composite of two projections. Its image lies in the compatible-family subspace $E_a$ for the cover of $W\cap U_a$; the same subbasis test makes the map to $E_a$ continuous. The assumed topological sheaf axiom of $\mathcal F_a$ gives a continuous inverse $E_a\to\mathcal F_a(W\cap U_a)$, so the $a$-coordinate of $\rho^{-1}$ is continuous. Step 1 now gives continuity into $\mathcal F(W)$. This verifies the full topological sheaf condition, not merely its underlying set version.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA: sheaf equalizer in topological rings; Tag 00AL construction

proof.text: For $W\subseteq U_a$, define $e_{a,W}(s)=s_a$. Its inverse sends $r\in\mathcal F_a(W)$ to the tuple with $b$-coordinate $\theta_{ab}(r|_{W\cap U_b})$. The cocycle identity $\theta_{bc}\theta_{ab}=\theta_{ac}$, after restriction to $W\cap U_b\cap U_c$, makes this tuple compatible; $\theta_{aa}=1$ makes its $a$-coordinate $r$. Conversely, compatibility of any tuple with index $a$ forces every $b$-coordinate to have exactly this formula. Both maps are unital ring homomorphisms, and both are continuous: projection is continuous and all coordinates of the inverse are continuous restrictions followed by continuous transition maps (step 1). Naturality follows from that of the restrictions and transitions. Thus these are isomorphisms of sheaves of topological rings. The defining tuple equation gives $\theta_{ab}e_a=e_b$ on overlaps.

source.place: Tag 00AL, lemma-glue-sheaves, first proof, last paragraph; Tag 0AHY topology

proof.text: Let $\alpha_a:\mathcal H|_{U_a}\to\mathcal G|_{U_a}$ be compatible local morphisms as in the statement. For $h\in\mathcal H(W)$ the sections $\alpha_a(h|_{W\cap U_a})$ agree on $W\cap U_a\cap U_b$: use naturality of $\alpha_a,\alpha_b$ and their assumed equality on that overlap. The sheaf axiom of $\mathcal G$ therefore gives a unique $\alpha_W(h)\in\mathcal G(W)$ with these restrictions. Applying this equality to $h+h'$, $hh'$, $-h$, $0$, and $1$ shows that $\alpha_W$ preserves the ring operations, by uniqueness of gluing. Restricting from $W$ to $W'$ gives the same restrictions as $\alpha_{W'}(h|_{W'})$, proving naturality by the same uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 00AN, lemma-mapping-property-glue, full faithfulness; explicit gluing of maps

proof.text: For the cover $W=\bigcup_a(W\cap U_a)$, write $E_{\mathcal G}$ for the compatible-family subspace of $\prod_a\mathcal G(W\cap U_a)$. The map $\mathcal H(W)\to E_{\mathcal G}$ used in step 7 is continuous: its $a$-coordinate is the continuous restriction of $\mathcal H$ followed by the continuous component of $\alpha_a$, so step 1 applies. The topological sheaf axiom of $\mathcal G$ identifies $E_{\mathcal G}$ homeomorphically with $\mathcal G(W)$, proving continuity of $\alpha_W$. Any extension must give exactly these local restrictions on every section, so separatedness of $\mathcal G$ proves uniqueness. This proves morphism descent including continuity.

source.place: Tag 00AN, lemma-mapping-property-glue, together with Tag 0AHY topological equalizer condition

proof.text: If $(\mathcal F',e'_a)$ is another descended sheaf with the specified transition identifications, the local maps $(e'_a)^{-1}e_a$ agree on overlaps, since $e_b=\theta_{ab}e_a$ and $e'_b=\theta_{ab}e'_a$. Steps 7--8 glue them and their inverses; the composites restrict to identities, hence are identities by uniqueness in those steps. This proves the asserted unique isomorphism. Finally, the empty-cover sheaf axiom forces every local sheaf's section ring on $\varnothing$ to be the one-element ring, homeomorphic to the empty product. If $A=\varnothing$ the cover condition forces $X=\varnothing$ and our tuple construction is that same one-element ring. If $X=\varnothing$ with nonempty $A$, every factor is a one-element ring, so the construction and every argument above still apply. Empty members, infinite covers, and repeated cover members require no extra hypothesis.
